evidence.source: Adam Khoo — US Stocks Crash? Midterm Election Rally Dead? (Nov 2)
evidence.claim: Post-midterm history: avg +8.1% over next 3 months, 95% positive (19 midterms, only 2018 negative); pre-election dips bottom Oct/early Nov seasonally
evidence.relation: election uncertainty resolves -> risk-on flows; seasonal pattern

evidence.claim: Hedge funds de-grossed -7.8% last week, biggest in 10 years; 6 prior >5% de-grossings all coincided with S&P lows and all were up 1/3/6 months later
evidence.relation: forced deleveraging exhausts sellers -> sell pressure dries up near bottom

evidence.claim: Q3 earnings +30.2% aggregate vs +29% expected; breadth broadening (non-Mag7 earnings growth 32% vs Mag7 22%); S&P net margin 17% (AI cost savings real)
evidence.relation: earnings breadth + margin expansion -> index-level earnings-driven returns

evidence.claim: S&P forward PE 18.7 vs 5yr avg 19.8 and 10yr avg 19.1; cheaper than Jan's 22x (earnings grew faster than price)
evidence.relation: below-average multiple -> less downside risk, earnings-driven upside

evidence.claim: His floor call: at worst a break to 716 (-8% from highs, below a correction), then rally to year-end and next year

resolution: Khoo's flow/positioning/seasonality evidence (de-grossing, midterms, breadth) argues near-bottom and conflicts with the market prior's very-bearish read (72% Dec hike, 74% ceasefire-break, 44.5% hot CPI). Resolution: the two describe different drivers — Khoo addresses market structure and earnings (short-term flows), not the Fed-rehike/CPI macro regime that the odds encode. We accept the flow evidence as shrinking the severity of downside (bearish, not very-bearish) while keeping policy/geopolitical risk as the dominant constraint. If the Dec hike materializes alongside hot CPI, seasonality historically loses to policy shocks (2018 analogue).
